title: EEG As a Genetic Selection Lever in Autism Spectrum Disorder
official: Electroencephalography in Autism Spectrum Disorder: A Potential Aid in the Selection of Candidates for Extended Genetic Testing
summary:
Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a growing public health concern, with genetic causes identified in about 20% of cases. While exome/genome sequencing is powerful, its cost and limited yield call for better patient selection.

Electroencephalography (EEG) shows promise: early EEG patterns can predict ASD, and specific EEG features may help identify subgroups more likely to have a genetic cause. This project explores using EEG to optimize genetic testing strategies in ASD.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Age \< 18 years
* Children with ASD
* Having undergone exome sequencing
* Having undergone a sleep EEG

Exclusion Criteria:

* Children whose legal representative has objected to the reuse of their data
* Presenting with another previously identified cause that may explain the ASD (toxic, infectious, perinatal distress)
